text: I'll walk to the rowboat to look inside and inspect the oar; I may pick it up if useful.
Examine the oar's condition and size to see if it's usable or could be useful as a tool.
I'll pick up the oar to carry it—could be useful for paddling or as a tool.
Check inside the rowboat for supplies, damage, or anything useful.
Walk to the shoreline to check the water, look for seaweed, shells, currents, or anything washed up.
Head to the driftwood log to inspect it for size, condition, and whether I can use it for shelter, firewood, or tools.
Grab the 3 ft driftwood to use as firewood or a tool, then I'll decide whether to go examine the nearby rope or crate.
Walk east to the coil of rope to inspect it and see if it's usable (length, condition). I'll check the nearby crate afterward.
Pick up the coil of rope (about 30 ft). I'll carry it — could be useful for climbing, hauling, or tying things; may consider using it on the ladder or to reach the platform later.
Set the driftwood down so one hand is free, then I'll pick up the coil of rope.
Pick up the coil of rope so I have it with the oar; then I'll consider heading toward the ladder/tower to inspect it.
Head to the tall metal ladder/tower to inspect it and check if I can climb up to the platform. I'll keep the oar and rope with me.
Let the walk continue to the ladder; once there I'll inspect the ladder and decide whether to climb with the rope/oar.
